epic.title: lh-episode-rewording
epic.intent_and_why: The episode-observation guard reds the suite on three offenders in launcher-hygiene-001/002/003; reword to green without shortening substance, without touching the guard, and without adding to its exception list.

definition_of_done: full clean-env suite shows 0 failed (other than the two named pre-existing Windows-only failures, N/A on this Linux worktree)
each statement's before/after text and the 002 (a)/(b) determination are recorded
changes committed and pushed to fix/launcher-hygiene

good_enough.mandatory_quality: Every word of substance in the three assertions survives; the store is only ever written through scripts/apply_episode_delta.py
good_enough.sufficient_evidence: Targeted guard test green plus full clean-env suite green

hard_constraints: The guard itself and its test file are not in scope
fixed_decisions: Work happens on the existing fix/launcher-hygiene branch, no second PR

current_wave.objective: Reword launcher-hygiene-001.a5, launcher-hygiene-002.a3, launcher-hygiene-003.a5 so the episode-observation guard passes, preserving substance.

issues.title: Restate the three offending assertions via apply_episode_delta.py
issues.desired_outcome: The episode-observation guard passes on episodes/active/launcher-hygiene-00{1,2,3}.md with no substance lost.
issues.useful_now: It is the only thing blocking PR #591, whose code is otherwise finished, correct, and verified.
issues.acceptance_or_falsification_evidence: python -m pytest -q tests/test_episode_observations.py and the full clean-env suite both pass
issues.implementation_latitude: Choose the minimal reword per statement; 002.a3's (a)/(b) determination is this run's own call, made against the guard's own regex, not guessed
hard_constraints_no_gos: No edit to scripts/verify_episode_observations.py or tests/test_episode_observations.py

completed_outcomes.outcome: Restated launcher-hygiene-001.a5 and launcher-hygiene-003.a5 by adding an explicit subject before the clause-opening bare imperative ('read'/'Read'); restated launcher-hygiene-002.a3 by switching both verbatim excerpts from single to double quotes only, with no word changed, per the (a) determination that the guard's existing quoted-machine-output carve-out already covers this shape but its single-quote pairing regex breaks internally on the excerpt's own verbatim 'you're'.
completed_outcomes.evidence: python scripts/apply_episode_delta.py --delta .agent-work/lh-episode-rewording/reword-delta.json applied cleanly (dry-run verified first); python -m pytest -q tests/test_episode_observations.py green; full clean-env suite green.

wave_evidence.claim: The episode-observation guard reds RealStoreTests on exactly launcher-hygiene-001.a5, -002.a3, -003.a5 before this run.
wave_evidence.observed: python -m pytest -q tests/test_episode_observations.py showed 2 failed before the reword, 0 failed after

wave_evidence.claim: 002.a3's flagged second-person 'you' originates inside a verbatim-quoted excerpt, not the record addressing a reader.
wave_evidence.expected: The existing carve-out (test_second_person_inside_a_quotation_is_not_flagged) should exempt it
wave_evidence.observed: Direct call to the guard's own second_person_hits()/triggers_for() showed the single-quote pairing regex fails to strip the second excerpt because its own verbatim 'you're' breaks the delimiter's letter-boundary guard; switching to double quotes (no word changed) restores the exemption, verified with triggers_for() returning []
wave_evidence.source: scripts/verify_episode_observations.py (direct interactive verification against its regex, this run)

discrepancies.signal: scripts/apply_episode_delta.py's restate-assertion op fully expressed all three restatements; no hand-edit of episode markdown was needed.
discrepancies.affects: LAUNCH_ORDER's conditional instruction to hand-edit only if the delta tool could not express the restatement
discrepancies.evidence: python scripts/apply_episode_delta.py --delta .agent-work/lh-episode-rewording/reword-delta.json (dry-run and real run both succeeded for all three ops)
discrepancies.reason: Recorded so the launch order's own contingency is known to be moot for this run; no issue warranted.

discrepancies.signal: scripts/verify_episode_observations.py's single-quote span regex ((?<![A-Za-z])'[^']*'(?![A-Za-z])) fails to pair a legitimately quoted excerpt when the excerpt's own verbatim text contains a letter-adjacent apostrophe (e.g. "you're"), because the pairing search treats that internal apostrophe as a candidate delimiter and fails the lookahead/lookbehind guard on both sides.
discrepancies.affects: Future episode records that verbatim-quote machine text containing a contraction or possessive, using single quotes
discrepancies.evidence: Reproduced directly: g.second_person_hits() on the pre-reword launcher-hygiene-002.a3 statement returns ['you'] sourced from the second (unpaired) quoted span, not the first; reworking the excerpt to double quotes makes triggers_for() return [] with zero wording change.
discrepancies.reason: The guard and its test file are explicitly out of scope for this run (LAUNCH_ORDER File Ownership); recorded as a finding for Triage rather than fixed here. Double-quoting is a viable house convention going forward for any verbatim excerpt containing an apostrophe, but that is a decision for the guard's owner, not this run.
